settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: The resolver only follows refs that literally appear in the supplied document or in documents it has already loaded; it does not enumerate the filesystem.
INTERNAL refs bypass file access entirely, so only explicit external refs are affected.
Reads are bounded by the process's file permissions, and content is not returned to the attacker unless the caller serializes/exposes the resolved model.
No end-to-end caller inside this repository demonstrates an attacker-controlled ref reaching the resolver in a network-service context.
candidates.description: When resolving an external RELATIVE ref, RefUtils.readExternalRef resolves the ref string against the parent directory of the parsed document without any containment or allow-list check: `final Path pathToUse = parentDirectory.resolve(file).normalize();` and, if the resolved path exists, reads it with `IOUtils.toString(new FileInputStream(pathToUse.toFile()), "UTF-8")`. A `$ref` value such as `../../../../etc/passwd#/anything` embedded in a parsed Swagger document therefore causes the parser to read a file outside the document's directory and embed its contents into the in-memory model (and, depending on the caller, into returned/reserialized output). If the resolved local path does not exist, the code falls back to `ClasspathHelper.loadFileFromClasspath(file)`, which uses getResourceAsStream/getClassLoader().getResourceAsStream/getSystemResourceAsStream on the same attacker-influenced string, allowing reads of classpath resources. No normalization-based boundary check, sandboxing option, or user confirmation is visible in this path. This is a path-traversal / arbitrary-file-read primitive in a library typically fed untrusted API descriptions. Impact depends entirely on how the embedding application handles and exposes the resolved model.
missing_evidence: No end-to-end caller in this repository shows an externally reachable path where attacker-controlled input reaches RefUtils.readExternalRef.
The snippet range read does not show whether any option (e.g. a resolve/resolveFully flag or a pre-validation filter) restricts external refs before this method runs.
Impact depends on unknown downstream handling of the resolved model.
preconditions: The application parses a Swagger/OpenAPI description whose contents (or whose referenced documents) an attacker can influence.
The application runs the resolver over that input (e.g. SwaggerParser.readWithInfo/read with resolve enabled, or SwaggerResolver.resolve) so that external refs are processed.
The process has read permission on the target file
The application exposes the resolved model (or resolved file contents) to the attacker, or the read otherwise affects behavior the attacker can observe.
candidates.title: Arbitrary local file read via unvalidated relative external $ref (path traversal) in RefUtils.readExternalRef
